title: Design a requirements map, strategy view and roadmap from BRIEF.md
summary: One new design doc, docs/design/requirements-map.md. It maps every BRIEF.md requirement, addenda included, to a status, an owning design and serving jobs. It also specifies the living strategy view (A1) and a roadmap that orders the queued work. Design only: no code, no schema implementation, and BRIEF.md is untouched.

defaults_applied.how: Alternatives, tradeoffs and a pending independent review are included.
Each status and claim cites a file, or is labeled design or estimate.
Written so an outside reader can follow it without the brief.
Read the brief, addenda and existing designs to recover the request's scope.

assumptions: Queued work means the proposed designs under docs/design/ (parallel-jobs, native-pr-landing, squash-chain-landing, study-capability-m1) plus items implied by the addenda. Job ids can only be cited from files visible in the repo; records/ is absent, so serving jobs may be listed by design doc or request.
The map is a Markdown design doc that specifies a structured data form (fields and generated views) without implementing it.
The strategy view is specified here as a design only. Its live instance comes later through Athena.

acceptance_criteria.text: docs/design/requirements-map.md exists and states its status as proposed, with the independent review pending, in the style of the existing docs/design/*.md files.

It has a requirements table with one row for every ID in BRIEF.md: O1-O5, A1-A13, S1-S7, D1-D3, and the 2026-10-10 to 2026-10-13 addenda (plugin, taste probes, project tracker, native PR handling, brownfield and stealth, brief as structured contract, tired user and artifact home, dashboard, chunking and parallelism, job-state reconstruction and retros, acceleration). Each row has a status from a defined vocabulary, an owning design doc and the serving jobs.
Every owning-design cell names a file that exists under docs/ or says 'none yet'. Serving jobs are referenced by job id or by the queued request, and no id is invented.

It specifies the living strategy view (A1) with goals, bets, risks, open questions and next steps, and says how each part is sourced from the map and kept current. It also covers pushback and the recorded exchange. It names the data shape (structured fields) and how it is regenerated.

It has a roadmap that sequences the queued work, with each item's dependencies and rationale. The queued work includes the parallel-jobs, native-pr-landing, squash-chain-landing and study-capability-m1 designs and the brief-derived items. The roadmap honors the BRIEF.md order (M1 on firstmate before the study broadens) and the addenda on moving the study up.

It lists alternatives considered (for example a hand-written table against a structured file with generated views, and where Jev is used cheaply for tracing) and the tradeoffs. It states what is out of scope, and notes that BRIEF.md is never edited.
Claims are marked read or design, and any count or status is cited to a file or labeled as an estimate.

Run `git status` and `git diff --stat`: only the listed docs paths changed, with no Rust, Cargo, CI or governance file touched and BRIEF.md unmodified. Run `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo test` to confirm nothing else broke.

out_of_scope: Any Rust code, schema files, or generators for the map or strategy view
Building the dashboard, project tracker, taste probes or any queued design
Changes to athena.toml, defaults.toml, CI or lint configuration
Reviewing or accepting the other designs
departures: The doc must cover about 40 requirements and cross-reference 4 existing designs, so it is somewhat larger than a typical doc job. Costs run slightly above the reference.
